title: Hurewicz Whitehead Freudenthal and Cw Approximation

items.title: Compact CW images have finite cell support without choice
items.statement: For every compact topological space K and continuous map f:K to a CW complex X with supplied characteristic maps, f(K) lies in a finite CW subcomplex. No choice principle is used: each occupied cell receives a canonical point from a compact coordinate slice by successive minima.
items.strategy: The image is compact by pulling back covers and is closed in the Hausdorff CW complex. In each occupied cell take the least nested inner characteristic ball meeting the image, and its lexicographically minimal preimage, constructed by finitely many extrema on compact slices. The selected image points form a closed discrete compact subspace by closure finiteness and the weak topology, hence are finite. Close the finite set of occupied cells downward in dimension.

references.title: Hatcher Appendix A, Proposition A.1 and its finite-subcomplex consequence; canonical coordinate selection replaces the usual unspecified point family

items.title: A low-dimensional disk can be pushed off a higher cell
items.statement: Let Z be a finite CW complex obtained from a subcomplex W by attaching one k-cell. If 0<=n<k, every map I^n to Z is homotopic, fixing the inverse image of W, to a map into W. The construction is choice-free and works with nonregular attaching maps.
items.strategy: Use nested coordinate balls in the open cell, a finite cubical mesh and compatible conical triangulations to interpolate only near the smaller ball. The interpolated image there lies in finitely many affine n-planes, while the image outside stays uniformly away from its center. Choose one omitted point, then use the explicit radial retraction of its punctured characteristic disk, descending through the attachment quotient.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Lemma 4.10 and proof of Theorem 4.8, pp.349–351

items.title: Cellular approximation for maps of CW pairs
items.statement: Let (X,A) and (Y,B) be CW pairs and let f:(X,A) to (Y,B) be continuous and cellular on A. If X minus A has finitely many cells, then f is homotopic rel A through maps of pairs to a cellular map g, meaning g(X^n) is contained in Y^n for every n, without any choice principle. Assuming the Axiom of Choice, the same conclusion holds for an arbitrary set of relative cells. Likewise, two cellular maps homotopic rel A are cellularly homotopic rel A; this is choice-free for a finite relative source and uses AC for an arbitrary one, after giving X times I its product CW structure.
items.strategy: Use the fully authored compact-image and finite cubical disk-avoidance lemmas to deform a characteristic n-disk rel its boundary into the target n-skeleton. Assemble cell deformations with the weak topology and exponential law and extend by the choice-free CW HEP. Finite relative cells require finite selections and finitely many stages. AC supplies a selection function on the set of all available disk deformation problems for arbitrary relative cells; the HEP itself is explicit. An eventually stationary infinite concatenation is continuous by transposing on each closed cell. Prove the product CW structure and apply the relative conclusion to a specified homotopy cylinder, fixing its ends and A cylinder.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem 4.8 and Lemma 4.10; May Chapter 10 §4

items.title: Each homotopy representative is supported on a finite CW subcomplex
items.statement: Every map from a compact sphere or disk into a CW complex has image in a finite subcomplex; every specified homotopy between such maps has image in a finite subcomplex. If the chosen basepoint is a 0-cell, the finite-source clause of cellular approximation gives a representative of pi_n(X) landing in X^n. No such based skeletal claim is made for a basepoint outside X^n, and no single finite subcomplex is asserted to contain all representatives.
items.strategy: Apply the compact-image corollary to S^n, D^n, and their products with I. These are finite CW sources, so the choice-free finite-source clause of cellular approximation gives skeletal dimension control while fixing a 0-cell basepoint. State both the basepoint restriction and the quantifiers per representative to avoid an illicit finite-CW reduction for the whole group.

references.title: Hatcher Appendix A and Theorem 4.8

items.title: Cellular attachments with finite boundary support form a CW complex
items.statement: Starting with a supplied CW complex A, attach a set of zero-cells and then, for each k>=1, a set of k-cells whose supplied attaching maps land in the preceding space (k-1)-skeleton and meet finitely many cells. The weak attachment topology on the union is a CW topology, A and every stage embed as closed subcomplexes, and compatible maps on A and all characteristic disks define continuous maps from the union. This requires no choice principle.
items.strategy: Prove the final topology tests all old and new characteristic disks and preserves closed subsets of earlier stages. Construct real functions separating two specified points by a dimension-recursive radial extension on every disk, with finite explicit interior bumps at the marked points; this proves Hausdorffness without choice. The finite boundary support gives closure finiteness. A finite closed-cell argument verifies the skeleton attachment topology.

references.title: Hatcher, expanded Appendix A, Proposition A.2, pp.3–4; local choice-free separation construction

items.title: CW approximation of an arbitrary space
items.statement: For every space X there is a CW complex Gamma X and a map gamma:Gamma X to X inducing a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on pi_n at every basepoint for all n>=1. A CW approximation of a pair can extend a prescribed approximation of its subspace. This construction uses no AC: attachments are indexed by all actual maps and all actual nullhomotopy data rather than by selected representatives of homotopy classes, and only the finite-source clause of cellular approximation is used to test a sphere, disk, or homotopy.
items.strategy: Start relative to any prescribed CW map P to X, adjoining one vertex for every point of X. At stage k attach one k-cell for every actual cellular map of its boundary into the previous stage and every actual extension of its composite to a disk in X. Compact finite support and the local assembly lemma prove each stage and the union are CW. Stored disk maps define the map to X. Constant boundary data realize all homotopy classes; all actual nullhomotopy data kill the kernel after finite-source cellular approximation. Actual paths prove bijection on components. Radial paths to vertices and natural basepoint transport give every basepoint. Class-function recursion in ZF accounts for growing sets of data without AC.

references.title: Hatcher Proposition 4.13; May Chapter 10 §5

items.title: Cubical pinch is additive on relative homology
items.statement: For the based sphere pair (Q,R)=(I^n/boundary I^n,*) with n>=1, or the relative disk pair (Q,R)=(I^n/J,F/(F intersect J)) with n>=2, the coordinate-one pinch c:Q to Q wedge Q sends every alpha in H_n(Q,R;Z) to i1(alpha)+i2(alpha). Thus postcomposition with two based maps of pairs adds their induced homology values. Here F is the last-coordinate-zero face and J is the union of the other faces.
items.strategy: Prove the two-summand relative homology decomposition using the triple chain short exact sequence and CW excision, with the two collapse projections as its explicit inverse. The projections after coordinate pinch are induced by min(2t1,1) and max(2t1-1,0); interpolation with t1 gives pair homotopies to identity, preserving J exactly when the relative degree is at least two. Therefore pinch sends any class diagonally, giving additivity.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Proposition4.36, pp369–370, with the relative wedge splitting and cube reparametrizations supplied locally

items.title: Absolute and relative Hurewicz homomorphisms
items.statement: For n>=1, h:pi_n(X,x_0) to H_n(X;Z) sends [f:S^n to X] to f_*([S^n]) for the fixed positive orientation. For n>=2, h:pi_n(X,A,x_0) to H_n(X,A;Z) sends [f:(D^n,boundary D^n,s_0) to (X,A,x_0)] to f_*([D^n,boundary D^n]). These maps are natural, well-defined, and homomorphisms; changing the chosen orientation changes both by a common sign.
items.strategy: Define the oriented pushforwards and prove their well-definedness in a numbered verification. Use sphere homology and disk pair exactness to obtain the generators, the actual subspace-preserving prism to handle arbitrary target pairs, and the authored cubical-pinch identity for additivity. For the absolute n=1 comparison with point-relative homology, prove H0(point) injects by the retraction to a point. Naturality is composition of chain maps; reversing both orientation generators gives a common minus sign.

references.title: Hatcher Proposition 4.36 and preceding definition; May Chapter 15 §1

items.title: The first Hurewicz map is abelianization
items.statement: For every path-connected space X, h:pi_1(X,x_0) to H_1(X;Z) is surjective and has kernel the commutator subgroup. Hence pi_1(X,x_0)_ab is naturally isomorphic to H_1(X;Z). No local simple-connectivity or CW hypothesis is required.
items.strategy: Prove the actual path-chain relations with an affine singular triangle, constant simplices and endpoint-fixed prism homotopies. Identify the positively traversed circle with its oriented triangle-boundary generator. For one finite cycle choose paths only to its finitely many vertices, sum the corresponding based loops in the abelianization, and prove independence using boundary cancellation. The three edges of a singular triangle give the relation killing every boundary. This defines a choice-free inverse to the factored Hurewicz map and proves the precise kernel.

references.title: Hatcher Hurewicz discussion §2.A/§4.2; May Chapter 15 §1

items.title: Weak homotopy equivalence
items.statement: A continuous map f:X to Y is a weak homotopy equivalence if pi_0(f) is bijective and, for every x in X and n>=1, f_*:pi_n(X,x) to pi_n(Y,f(x)) is an isomorphism. This includes all components and all source basepoints; it is not defined merely by choosing one basepoint.
items.strategy: This records the exact Whitehead hypothesis directly in terms of path components and the already-defined based higher homotopy groups. Quantifying over every source basepoint avoids silently importing a basepoint-change theorem or omitting components.

references.title: Hatcher §4.1; May Chapter 10 §3

items.title: A weak equivalence has vanishing mapping-cylinder relative groups
items.statement: If f:X to Y is a weak homotopy equivalence, then for its mapping-cylinder inclusion j:X to M_f, every relative pi_n(M_f,X,x) is trivial for n>=1 and pi_0(X) to pi_0(M_f) is bijective. Conversely these conditions imply that f is a weak equivalence.
items.strategy: Construct the ordinary mapping cylinder for arbitrary spaces, prove both ends are closed embedded subspaces by testing closed inverse images, and descend its height deformation through the quotient times I. The deformation fixes the target basepoint; the track from each source point and moving-basepoint transport prove that the retraction induces isomorphisms at source basepoints as well. Apply the pair exact sequence in both directions, treating the pointed relative degree-one tail explicitly and retaining component bijectivity separately.

references.title: Hatcher proof of Theorem 4.5

items.title: Vanishing relative homotopy extends an inverse over cells
items.statement: Let i:X to Z be a cellular inclusion of CW complexes with all relative homotopy groups trivial and a component bijection. If Z minus X has finitely many cells, then choice-free obstruction extension gives r:Z to X with r i=id_X and a homotopy i r homotopic to id_Z rel X. Assuming the Axiom of Choice, the same conclusion holds for arbitrary cell sets and unbounded dimension.
items.strategy: Compress each characteristic disk rel its boundary using relative nullity at its actual marked boundary image; use component-surjectivity for vertices. Glue on X union the current skeleton, extend by the explicit CW HEP, and concatenate homotopies stationary on each closed cell after finitely many stages. Finite relative cells require only finite selections. In the arbitrary case use one AC selector on all actual disk-compression and point-path problems, then specified recursion. The endpoint factors continuously through the subspace X and fixes it pointwise.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Lemma 4.6 and the subcomplex case of Theorem 4.5, printed pp.346–347

items.title: Cellular mapping cylinders and relative cylinders are CW complexes
items.statement: Let X and Y be CW complexes with a common CW subcomplex A, and f:X to Y cellular with f restricted to A the identity. The ordinary quotient W of Y disjoint X times I by (x,0)~f(x) and (a,t)~a is a CW complex with X and Y as subcomplexes meeting in A. Its cells are those of Y, those of X outside A, and one (r+1)-cell for each r-cell of X outside A. The height deformation strongly retracts W onto Y, fixing A, and its retraction is an isomorphism on components and every based homotopy group. For A empty this is the ordinary mapping cylinder. The construction and finite-cell count use no choice.
items.strategy: First assemble the amalgamated endpoint CW complex Y union_A X using the supplied cells of X outside A. Attach characteristic prisms in ascending dimension; their side boundaries use earlier prisms, and cellularity bounds the bottom image dimension. Finite boundary support and the assembly lemma give a genuine CW complex. Identify its topology with the ordinary quotient by testing maps on X characteristic prisms using the interval exponential law. The explicit height homotopy descends through the extra A-track relation and gives the strong deformation, with moving-basepoint transport proving all based isomorphisms.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, proof of Theorem4.5 p347 and Proposition4.15 pp353–354; ordinary CW topology and relative cylinder details supplied locally

items.title: Whitehead theorem
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every weak homotopy equivalence f:X to Y between CW complexes is a homotopy equivalence. If X and Y are finite CW complexes, the same conclusion follows without AC.
items.strategy: Cellularly approximate f and use each actual homotopy track to preserve the weak-equivalence condition at every source point. The fully authored cylinder lemma makes its ordinary mapping cylinder a CW pair, with a finite number of relative cells in the finite case. The relative-vanishing criterion and cell-compression lemma give a retraction onto X. Composing this with the target endpoint inclusion yields an explicit inverse; the two cylinder homotopies verify both composites. Transfer the inverse back along f homotopic to g, accounting for AC only in arbitrary-source approximation and arbitrary-cell compression.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem 4.5; May Whitehead Theorem, Chapter 10 §3

items.title: A weakly contractible CW complex is contractible
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A nonempty CW complex with one path component and pi_n(X,x)=0 for every n>=1 is contractible. For a finite CW complex the conclusion is choice-free.
items.strategy: The unique map X to a point is a weak equivalence by the hypotheses. Both spaces are CW complexes, so Whitehead makes it a homotopy equivalence, exactly a contraction of X.

references.title: Hatcher Whitehead theorem consequence; May Chapter 10 §3

items.title: Connectivity of a CW pair
items.statement: For k>=0 a CW pair (X,A) is k-connected if every path component of X meets A and pi_i(X,A,a) is trivial for every a in A and 1<=i<=k. Equivalently every map (D^i,S^{i-1}) to (X,A), 0<=i<=k, can be homotoped into A fixing its full boundary, with the zero-disk clause meaning a path to A. No relative pi0 is introduced and no choice is needed.
items.strategy: State component-surjectivity separately and use the actual marked boundary image to apply the disk-compression equivalence for each positive disk. The zero-disk case is exactly existence of a path into A. Conversely apply the fixed-boundary compression criterion to every relative representative at each basepoint.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, printed p346, equivalent definitions of relative connectivity

items.title: High relative cells do not change lower homotopy
items.statement: If (X,A) is a CW pair with all cells of X outside A in dimensions at least n>=1, then every map I^i to X for 0<=i<n deforms into A fixing the inverse image of A. Consequently the pair is (n-1)-connected, pi0(A) to pi0(X) is surjective and bijective for n>=2, and at every a in A the map pi_i(A,a) to pi_i(X,a) is an isomorphism for 1<=i<n-1 and a surjection for i=n-1>=1. No vertex restriction or choice principle is required.
items.strategy: Place each given compact cube map in a finite subcomplex, then remove a highest-dimensional cell outside A one at a time. Its complement remains a subcomplex even when A contains higher-dimensional cells, because A is a subcomplex. Each avoidance fixes the original inverse image of A. Apply the finite cube argument to based representatives, based nullhomotopies and paths, preserving all required boundary data.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Corollary4.9, Lemma4.10 and the cell-attachment argument on pp351–353; relative compact-domain proof supplied locally

items.title: Weak homotopy equivalences induce integral homology isomorphisms without choice
items.statement: Every weak homotopy equivalence of arbitrary topological spaces induces isomorphisms on integral singular homology in all nonnegative degrees, without choice. A map of pairs that is weak on both the total spaces and the subspaces induces relative integral homology isomorphisms as well.
items.strategy: Compress one finite CW domain at a time using relative disk compression and explicit HEP. Construct that domain from the finite face-closed collection of singular simplices in a relative cycle. The prism identity proves vanishing in a weak mapping cylinder. Its pair sequence gives the absolute comparison; a complete natural pair-sequence diagram chase gives the relative comparison.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Lemma4.6 pp346–347 and Proposition4.21 pp356–357; complete proofs read, finite-choice and finite face-realization details supplied locally

items.title: A connected CW pair has a model without low relative cells
items.statement: Let n>=1 and (X,A) be an (n-1)-connected CW pair with A nonempty. Choice-free, there is a CW complex Z containing A, with only relative cells of dimensions at least n, and a weak homotopy equivalence Q:Z to X equal to the identity on A. Assuming AC, Q is a homotopy equivalence rel A, with inverse and both homotopies fixed on A. The construction of the weak model itself uses no choice.
items.strategy: Start from A with no extra vertices and attach k-cells for k>=n indexed by all actual cellular boundaries and disk extensions into X. Pair exactness supplies the initial lower isomorphisms and endpoint surjection; high-cell avoidance preserves the lower groups. Constant-boundary disks supply high-degree surjectivity and all nullhomotopy extension data kill kernels after finite-source cellular approximation. Handle pi0 separately, including n=1, and transport from vertices naturally. Under AC make Q cellular rel A, use the fully proved relative CW cylinder, derive relative vanishing by exactness, and apply cell compression. Explicit endpoint composites give an inverse and homotopies fixed on A.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Proposition4.15 pp353–354 and construction on pp352–353; all-data choice-free weak model and relative inverse details supplied locally

items.title: Finite relative homotopy lifting across a weak equivalence
items.statement: Let f:P to Y be a weak homotopy equivalence of arbitrary spaces and (K,L) a CW pair with finitely many cells outside L. Given u:L to P, v:K to Y and T:L times I to Y from v restricted to L to fu, there are w:K to P extending u and J:K times I to Y from v to fw with J(l,t)=T(l,min(4t,1)). In particular strict commuting data have a lift up to homotopy rel L. No choice is needed even for infinite L.
items.strategy: Use the ordinary mapping cylinder and HEP to deform kv until its L-values equal ju, following T then the source cylinder track. Its relative groups vanish by the weak-equivalence criterion. Compress the resulting map into P one finite-relative source cell at a time using full-boundary relative disk compression and HEP on K. Compose the concatenated homotopy with the cylinder retraction; on L the precise time schedule gives T(l,min(4t,1)).

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter10 §3 HELP, p75; Hatcher Lemma4.6 p347; finite-relative ordinary-space proof with explicit time schedule

items.title: Weak equivalences glue along a common connected CW subcomplex
items.statement: Let X=A union_C B be a CW union with C nonempty path-connected and (A,C),(B,C) zero-connected. Let P_A,P_B be CW complexes containing the same C and let q_A:P_A to A and q_B:P_B to B be weak equivalences equal to the identity on C. Then P=P_A union_C P_B is CW and the glued map q:P to X is a weak equivalence. No choice principle is used; cellular approximation and lifting are applied only to CW pairs with finitely many cells outside C.
items.strategy: Surjectivity factors a compact cube image through C plus finitely many target cells, then uses finite relative HELP on each side rel C. For injectivity put a source representative in C plus finitely many source cells, cellularly approximate each restricted q rel C, and retain a finite target enlargement containing all homotopy images and the nullhomotopy. Its relative cylinder splits into two finite-relative CW pairs. Finite HELP with the prescribed approximation tracks yields a map of that cylinder into P extending the source inclusion. The original representative is null in the cylinder and hence in P. Transport from one point of C proves all-basepoint weak equivalence.

references.title: May, A Concise Course, Chapter11 §3 p87, weak CW-triad reduction; Chapter10 §3 p75 HELP; finite-data proof supplied locally

items.title: Weak equivalences of pairs induce isomorphisms on relative homotopy
items.statement: Let f:(X,A) to (Y,B) be a map of pairs whose ambient map f and restriction g:A to B are weak homotopy equivalences. For every a in A the induced relative map is a pointed bijection in degree one and a group isomorphism in every degree n>=2. The spaces and subspaces are arbitrary. No choice principle is required.
items.strategy: Lift the boundary of a relative cube along g, fixed on J; extend the resulting boundary homotopy over the cube and lift the adjusted cube along f. For injectivity first lift the side of a given relative homotopy along g, fixing endpoint boundaries and J tracks. Extend the resulting boundary homotopy over the whole cube cylinder and lift the adjusted cylinder along f, fixing its entire prescribed boundary. Every lifting source is finite cubical CW, so no AC is used. This proves equality of arbitrary classes, including the pointed degree-one case.

references.title: May, A Concise Course, Chapter10 §3 pp75–76, HELP and its cylinder proof of injectivity; relative cubical version proved here

items.title: Homotopy excision for a single relative cell layer
items.statement: Let X=A union B be a CW union with C=A intersection B and specified c in C. Suppose A is obtained from C by finitely many cells, each of dimension at least a>=1 and with its entire attaching boundary in C. Suppose B is obtained from C by finitely many relative cells of dimensions at least b>=1. Then pi_i(A,C,c) to pi_i(X,B,c) is an isomorphism for 1<=i<a+b-2 and surjective for positive i=a+b-2. The common C may be infinite or disconnected. No choice principle is required.
items.strategy: Regularize a cube locally inside each open attached cell by a finite mesh and affine interpolation. Shrink coordinate cubes away from all deficient-rank simplex images. Fibres over the B-cell have dimension at most d-b; their vertical saturation has dimension at most d-b+1<a. Select finitely many A-cell points outside its affine images. A distance cutoff produces a graph above the B fibre and below the A fibres. Reparametrize the last cube coordinate above this graph. Punctured-cell radial deformations and relative weak-equivalence comparison identify the changed pairs with the original ones. Apply the same construction to a relative homotopy, fixing its endpoint parameter via the graph. Remove multiple B cells in decreasing dimension by composition of the one-cell conclusions.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Lemma4.10 pp350–351 and Theorem4.23 proof Cases1–2 pp361–362; explicit rank, graph and pair comparisons supplied here

items.title: Relative homotopy exact sequence of a triple in group degrees
items.statement: For c in A subset B subset X, the sequence pi_{n+1}(X,B) to pi_n(B,A) to pi_n(X,A) to pi_n(X,B) to pi_{n-1}(B,A) is natural and exact at its three middle terms for n>=2. The boundary is the pair boundary into absolute pi_n(B) followed by the relative map into pi_n(B,A). All arrows between displayed group degrees are homomorphisms; the final target for n=2 is a pointed set. No exactness after that target or relative degree-zero assertion is included. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: At pi_n(B,A), use naturality and the pair sequence to lift a kernel class to an absolute B class, subtract its absolute A preimage in X, then use the (X,B) boundary. At pi_n(X,A), relative nullity in (X,B) compresses the disk into B fixing its boundary in A. At pi_n(X,B), relative nullity of its absolute B boundary compresses that boundary into A fixing its whole boundary; a shrinking bottom collar adjusts the cube accordingly. This establishes the precise group-degree triple segment used by the cell-layer induction.

references.title: May, A Concise Course, Chapter11 §3 p86, triple sequence; Hatcher Theorem4.23 Case3 p363. Complete group-degree proof supplied locally.

items.title: Homotopy excision
items.statement: Let X=A union B be a CW complex, with A,B subcomplexes and nonempty path-connected C=A intersection B. If (A,C) is m-connected and (B,C) is n-connected, m,n>=0, then for positive degrees the map pi_i(A,C,c) to pi_i(X,B,c) is an isomorphism for i<m+n and a surjection for i=m+n, at every c in C. In degree one isomorphism means pointed bijection. When m+n=0 the positive-degree range is empty; no relative pi0 is asserted. No choice principle is required.
items.strategy: Prove the no-low-cell case first. Handle relative pi1 by high-cell control and the explicit path-prefix criterion for relative loop classes. With finitely many relative cells, induct over A layers using the fully proved single-layer excision lemma and the relative triple segment, spelling out the nonabelian group chase and its pointed final target. Compact support passes to arbitrary relative cell sets. Replace each original pair by its choice-free no-low-cell weak model; weak-equivalence gluing and relative weak-comparison give a commuting square with vertical bijections. Only the weak-model clause is used, not its AC homotopy inverse.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem 4.23 and full proof; May Chapter 11 §§1--3

items.title: CW quotients and collapse of a contractible subcomplex
items.statement: For a CW pair (X,A) with A nonempty, the ordinary quotient X/A is CW with one new vertex and one cell of the same dimension for every cell of X outside A. If A has a contraction, the quotient map q:X to X/A is a homotopy equivalence and a weak equivalence at all basepoints. If its supplied contraction fixes a in A, the constructed inverse and both homotopies are based at a and the quotient vertex. No choice is required; the contraction is one supplied witness.
items.strategy: Assemble the quotient CW from the new vertex and the remaining characteristic disks with their boundaries composed with collapse, and identify its map-out topology with the ordinary quotient. Extend the given contraction from A to X by choice-free HEP. Its endpoint factors as gq. The projected homotopy descends jointly across q times I, giving id to qg. The two homotopies commute with q; their moving-basepoint tracks give explicit inverse homomorphisms at every basepoint.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, quotient CW construction Chapter0 pp8–10 and Proposition0.17 pp15–16; ordinary topology and basepoint details supplied here

items.title: Relative homotopy compares with the CW quotient in the connectivity range
items.statement: Let (X,A) be an r-connected CW pair with r>=0, and let A be s-connected with s>=0. For every a in A the quotient induces pi_i(X,A,a) to pi_i(X/A,*) bijective for 1<=i<=r+s and surjective for i=r+s+1; these are group isomorphisms in degrees i>=2 and pointed bijections in degree one. No choice is required.
items.strategy: Build the ordinary cone as a cellular mapping cylinder to a point, and assemble Y=X union_A CA as a CW union. The pair LES makes (CA,A) (s+1)-connected, so homotopy excision gives the exact r+s range into (Y,CA). Collapse the contractible cone: the new quotient lemma and relative weak comparison identify all positive relative groups of (Y,CA) with the absolute groups of X/A. Universal quotient map-out tests show the latter quotient is literally X/A and the composite is its quotient-induced map.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Proposition4.28 p364; full CW and quotient comparisons supplied here

items.title: The first potentially nonzero homotopy group of a wedge of higher spheres has its cell basis
items.statement: For n>=2 and any set J, the CW wedge W of copies of S^n indexed by J has pi_i(W)=0 for 0<i<n, and pi_n(W) is free abelian on the based inclusions of those spheres. The inverse to the basis map sends a spherical representative u to the finitely supported vector of degrees deg(p_j u), where p_j collapses the other summands. The empty wedge is a point. No choice is used.
items.strategy: Construct the CW wedge from one vertex and the given sphere disks. For finite J prove the ordinary product of spheres has the finite product CW structure directly from characteristic cube products and compact closed-cell tests. Its cells outside the axes have dimension at least 2n, so the wedge inclusion induces pi_n isomorphism for n>=2. Coordinate maps and homotopies give the finite product group identification, and degree gives its integer basis. Compact finite cell support proves surjectivity and injectivity for arbitrary J and finite support of the coordinate degree vector.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Example4.26 p363; finite sphere-product topology and finite-support proof supplied locally

items.title: A CW quotient induces relative singular homology isomorphisms
items.statement: For every CW pair (X,A) with A nonempty, every abelian coefficient group G and every i>=0, the quotient map q induces an isomorphism H_i(X,A;G) to H_i(X/A,{*};G). This is the actual quotient-induced map and is natural in maps of pairs. The proof is choice-free and uses an explicit cylinder-end collar, not an assumed open retract neighborhood in X.
items.strategy: The ordinary cellular cylinder M of A->X has a free-end A_f with explicit open collar A times (1/2,1]. Good-pair quotient comparison gives H(M,A_f) isomorphic H(M/A_f,{v}). Retraction r:M->X and its identity on A induce a relative isomorphism by the pair sequences and an explicit group chase. The quotient M/A_f is Y=X union_A CA; its cone is a contractible CW subcomplex with a contraction fixing its apex. Collapsing that cone is a based homotopy equivalence by the local quotient lemma, hence a relative homology isomorphism by the prism formula. The maps commute q r=p q_M, identifying the resulting isomorphism with q_*.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Proposition2.22 and Proposition0.17 pp15–16; mapping-cylinder collar reduction supplied locally

items.title: Integral homology of a wedge of higher spheres has its cell basis
items.statement: For n>=2 and any set J, the CW wedge W of oriented n-spheres has H0(W;Z)=Z, Hn(W;Z)=direct sum_J Z with the inclusion orientation classes as basis, and all other positive homology zero. The inverse in degree n is given by the collapsing projections. The empty wedge is a point and the proof is choice-free.
items.strategy: For a finite wedge remove one sphere, retaining its basepoint in the remaining subcomplex U. The CW quotient W/U is that sphere. Quotient comparison and the positive-degree point-relative isomorphism identify the relative group with sphere homology. Retraction onto U is injective on homology and the last sphere inclusion splits the quotient map. The pair exact sequence gives the direct sum, with its coordinate projections. For an arbitrary wedge every finite singular cycle and every bounding chain is contained in a finite subwedge, proving surjectivity and injectivity. Path connectedness gives H0.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Example 2.23 and wedge homology; finite splitting supplied explicitly from the pair sequence

items.title: A relative single cell layer has compatible homotopy and homology bases
items.statement: Let A be a nonempty simply connected CW complex, a in A, and Z be obtained by attaching a set of oriented k-cells directly to A, k>=2. The groups pi_k(Z,A,a) and H_k(Z,A;Z) are free abelian on the characteristic cells, and relative Hurewicz sends each homotopy basis element to its homology basis element. The based characteristic class is obtained by moving the marked boundary value into a through A; it is independent of these choices. The construction is choice-free with supplied cell orientations.
items.strategy: The quotient Z/A is the wedge of the characteristic k-spheres. High-cell connectivity and simple connectivity of A put degree k in the relative quotient isomorphism range. The homotopy and homology wedge lemmas give bases. Use HEP first on the boundary sphere with a marked point and then on the disk to move a characteristic map to a based representative. Quotienting the homotopy keeps the whole collapsed boundary fixed, showing the relative class is uniquely the inverse of its wedge inclusion. Homotopy invariance and naturality of the relative Hurewicz pushforward identify its image with the characteristic relative orientation class. Quotient homology identifies these as the homology basis.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Example4.26, Proposition4.28 and the proof of Theorem4.32; based characteristic details supplied locally

items.title: Cellular reduction for a highly connected pair
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let (X,A) be an (n-1)-connected CW pair with n>=2 and A nonempty. It is homotopy equivalent rel A to a CW pair with no relative cells below n; cells above n+1 affect neither pi_n(X,A) nor H_n(X,A). If A is simply connected, the characteristic n-cells give free abelian bases for the relative n-skeleton groups, and after the (n+1)-cells are attached both full degree-n groups are cokernels of the identical integer incidence map under Hurewicz.
items.strategy: Use the completed no-low-cell model and its AC-dependent equivalence rel A. Derive the integral homology triple sequence from the actual relative chain quotients, compute each relative cell layer by CW quotient and sphere-wedge homology, and pass to arbitrary skeleta by finite cycles and bounding chains. This proves lower vanishing and high-cell homology stability without the incomplete published cellular suppliers. High-cell homotopy and the triple sequence prove pi_n stability. With simply connected A, the compatible single-layer bases apply to (Z_n,A) and (Z_n+1,Z_n). The two triple sequences give cokernels. Their columns are exactly the degrees of projections of the attaching maps, on homotopy by the wedge degree inverse and on homology by the boundary of the pushed relative orientation chain. Natural Hurewicz identifies the resulting cokernels.

references.title: Hatcher Proposition 4.15, proof of Theorem 4.32, and Lemma 4.38

items.title: Relative Hurewicz theorem in the simple-connectivity range
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let n>=2 and let (X,A,x_0) be an (n-1)-connected CW pair with A nonempty, path-connected and simply connected. Then H_i(X,A;Z)=0 for i<n and the relative Hurewicz homomorphism pi_n(X,A,x_0) to H_n(X,A;Z) is an isomorphism. For n=2 the hypotheses make the relative group abelian; without trivial pi_1(A)-action the general theorem requires a quotient and is not asserted here.
items.strategy: Use the completed cellular reduction, including its direct singular-homology lower vanishing and its identification of the actual Hurewicz map with the identity on the identical incidence cokernels. Spell out surjectivity and injectivity on representatives of these cokernels. Retain the CW-pair, simply connected A and AC hypotheses; do not consume the incomplete published cellular comparison or infer homology invariance from a weak CW approximation.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem 4.32 and proof; May Chapter 15 §1

items.title: Relative Hurewicz comparison through a choice-free weak model
items.statement: For an (n-1)-connected CW pair (X,A,a), n>=2, with A nonempty and simply connected, integral relative homology vanishes below n and the actual relative Hurewicz map in degree n is an isomorphism without choice. Use a supplied all-data weak model, without choosing a homotopy inverse of spaces.
items.strategy: Use the choice-free all-data no-low-cell weak model. Apply the proved choice-free cell computations on that supplied model, without the AC replacement step. The actual weak maps induce isomorphisms in relative homotopy and integral relative homology; naturality transfers the Hurewicz map and lower vanishing.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Proposition4.21 pp356–357 and proof of Theorem4.32 pp366–374; local weak-model comparison makes choice accounting explicit

items.title: Absolute Hurewicz theorem at the first nonzero degree
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the assertions in degrees n>=2. If a CW complex X is (n-1)-connected, then reduced H_i(X;Z)=0 for i<n and h:pi_n(X) to H_n(X;Z) is an isomorphism. For n=1 and path-connected X, the choice-free degree-one result says that h is abelianization. The corresponding conclusions transfer to spaces already known homotopy equivalent to CW complexes.
items.strategy: Apply relative Hurewicz at a CW vertex, explicitly identify point-relative homotopy and positive homology and their orientation-normalized Hurewicz maps, and prove reduced H0 separately. Extend to every basepoint using the actual moving-boundary radial-shell homotopy, which descends to an unbased sphere homotopy and preserves Hurewicz images. For an actual homotopy equivalence to a CW complex use transport and inverse homotopies to prove all-basepoint homotopy isomorphisms, prism invariance for homology, and the natural Hurewicz square. Keep the degree-one abelianization theorem choice-free for every path-connected based space.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Theorem4.32 pp366–367 and Hurewicz definition pp369–370; all-basepoint and actual CW-type transfer supplied locally

items.title: Double-mapping-cylinder homotopy pushout and path-space homotopy pullback
items.statement: For maps f:A to B and g:A to C of CGWH spaces, the double mapping cylinder P is the kified quotient of B disjoint-union (A times I) disjoint-union C by (a,0)~f(a) and (a,1)~g(a). It is the standard homotopy-pushout model. For maps u:B to P and v:C to P, the path-space homotopy pullback is the kified subspace B times^h_P C={(b,omega,c):omega(0)=u(b), omega(1)=v(c)} of B times C(I,P) times C. The canonical comparison sends a to (f(a), t maps to [a,t], g(a)). If a_0 is chosen in A, this comparison is based by using (f(a_0), t maps to [a_0,t], g(a_0)) as the pullback basepoint; no endpoint inclusion is falsely required to preserve one common basepoint in P. These constructions and the comparison are continuous and use no choice principle.
items.strategy: Construct P as one closed-end pushout of A times {0,1} into A times I, along the map with values in B disjoint-union C, so it is already CGWH. For the pullback take the two endpoint-equality closed subsets of the k-product using the closed k-diagonal of P. Identify their intersection with the stated kified ordinary subspace by the CG-source mapping criterion in both directions. Curry the cylinder path, check its endpoint equations, and lift its graph into that subspace by the same criterion. Use the actual cylinder track for the based comparison.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 10 §7 double mapping cylinder
Rezk, Proof of the Blakers--Massey theorem, §3

items.title: Blakers--Massey connectivity for a homotopy-pushout square
items.statement: Assume AC. For maps f:A to B and g:A to C of CW complexes respectively m-connected and n-connected in the relative-group convention, m,n>=1, the canonical cylinder-path comparison A to B times^h_P C for the double-mapping-cylinder homotopy pushout is (m+n-1)-connected. The source is A and each target basepoint includes its actual cylinder path. No choice is needed when f,g are cellular or when A is finite; AC is used only for cellular approximation of the two arbitrary maps.
items.strategy: Identify each based j-cube of the two mapping-path fibers with its actual relative (j+1)-cube, so excision gives the fiber comparison range. Prove component control and both total-space group directions by the natural fibration sequences. Build the cellular double cylinder as a CW union, retract its endpoint pullback using explicit whisker homotopies, and compare arbitrary maps to cellular representatives by explicit cylinder maps and inverse backtrack contractions, tracking the canonical comparison throughout.

references.title: Hatcher Theorem4.23 and complete local homotopy-excision proof; relative-cube to fiber and total-space comparisons derived explicitly here
Rezk §1.6 and Theorem3.1, connectivity convention and statement only; this item uses the classical excision proof, not Rezk's truncation proof

items.title: Freudenthal suspension theorem
items.statement: If X is an (n-1)-connected based CW complex with n>=1, suspension pi_i(X) to pi_{i+1}(Sigma X) is an isomorphism for i<2n-1 and a surjection for i=2n-1. Here Sigma X is the unreduced two-cone suspension based at one cone point, and the suspension homomorphism sends a based sphere map to its two-cone suspension.
items.strategy: Build the ordinary two-cone suspension as a CW union using cellular cylinders and CW quotients. Cone contractions and the pair LES give n-connectivity; homotopy excision gives the exact range. Collapse the lower contractible cone and use weak equivalence of pairs to compare the excision target to absolute groups. An explicit expanding-upper-disk homotopy proves that this comparison is exactly the two-cone suspension at its lower apex, including the basepoint distinction. No AC is used.

references.title: Hatcher Corollary 4.24; May Chapter 11 §2

title: Hurewicz Whitehead Freudenthal and Cw Approximation — Examples

items.title: First nonzero homotopy group of a sphere
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the Hurewicz proof when n>=2. For n>=1, pi_i(S^n)=0 for 0<i<n and pi_n(S^n) is isomorphic to Z. Under Hurewicz the identity sphere map goes to the positive fundamental class, so this is the degree isomorphism. The independently published degree classification gives the degree-n assertion choice-free.
items.strategy: Use the one-summand CW sphere calculation for lower connectivity, the exact absolute Hurewicz theorem for n>=2 and integral sphere homology. Evaluate the Hurewicz definition on the identity and on any degree-d representative. Treat n=1 directly by the already-proved degree classification. State the inherited AC cost only for the Hurewicz route; the independent sphere computation is choice-free.

references.title: Hatcher Corollary 4.25 and Theorem 4.32

items.title: Hurewicz calculation for a wedge of simply connected spheres
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For n>=2 and a nonempty finite set J, X=wedge_{j in J} S^n is (n-1)-connected and pi_n(X) is the free abelian group direct-sum_J Z generated by the wedge inclusions.
items.strategy: Check the finite CW wedge connectivity with the actual high-cell wedge supplier, use the proved integral wedge homology basis rather than the incomplete published cellular argument, and apply absolute Hurewicz. Evaluate natural Hurewicz on each inclusion and write the integer-coordinate forward and inverse maps, proving both compositions are identities. Retain the original AC hypothesis for this Hurewicz derivation and identify its inherited uses.

references.title: May Hurewicz wedge lemma, Chapter 15 §1

items.title: A simply connected CW homology equivalence is a homotopy equivalence under the stated choice conditions
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If f:X to Y is a map of simply connected CW complexes inducing isomorphisms on all integral homology groups, then f is a homotopy equivalence. If X and Y are finite CW complexes, the same conclusion is choice-free.
items.strategy: Cellularly approximate with the exact finite/AC clause, form the actual CW mapping cylinder, calculate every relative homology group from its pair sequence, and induct on relative homotopy vanishing using the choice-free weak-model Hurewicz comparison. Apply Whitehead with the finite/general clause and transfer both inverse homotopies to the original map.

references.title: Hatcher Corollary 4.33

items.title: Freudenthal stable range for spheres
items.statement: For n>=1, suspension pi_i(S^n) to pi_{i+1}(S^{n+1}) is an isomorphism for i<2n-1 and a surjection for i=2n-1. In particular pi_{n+k}(S^n) stabilizes under suspension once n>k+1.
items.strategy: S^n is (n-1)-connected, so substitute X=S^n in Freudenthal and use Sigma S^n homeomorphic to S^{n+1}. Writing i=n+k, the isomorphism condition n+k<2n-1 rearranges to n>k+1; equality gives only the endpoint surjection.

references.title: Hatcher Corollary 4.24; May Chapter 11 §2

items.title: Whitehead theorem fails without CW type
items.statement: Let Q_d be the rational numbers with the discrete topology and Q the rational subspace of R. The identity set map f:Q_d to Q is a weak homotopy equivalence but not a homotopy equivalence. Thus a CW-type hypothesis cannot be omitted from Whitehead's theorem.
items.strategy: Use irrational density and the intermediate value theorem to prove every rational-valued path is constant. Join any two cube points by their line segment to prove every positive-dimensional based cube into Q or Q_d is constant. Compute the component bijection pointwise. A homotopy inverse would be the identity set map Q to Q_d because every target homotopy has constant point tracks; rational density proves its singleton preimages are not open.

references.title: May Whitehead theorem hypotheses, Chapter 10 §3; explicit rational-space witness checked locally

items.title: A homology equivalence need not be a homotopy equivalence without simple connectivity
items.statement: Let X be the CW complex with one vertex, one-cells a,b, and one two-cell attached by a^2 b^{-3}. The map f:S^1 to X represented by the loop a b^{-1} is an integral homology equivalence but not a homotopy equivalence.
items.strategy: Compute the homology of the two-circle wedge by its split pair sequence, then use the actual CW quotient comparison for the single attached disk. Naturality of the pair boundary and degree-one Hurewicz additivity give the vector (2,-3), whose kernel and cokernel are computed explicitly. An actual annular van Kampen cover gives the presentation a^2=b^3 and its nonabelian S_3 quotient, ruling out homotopy equivalence. The incomplete published cellular-homology proof is not consumed.

references.title: Hatcher discussion after Corollary 4.33; explicit two-cell witness checked locally
